raw_response:
I am 74 years old. I have been farming my land in Quzhou for 50 years, and my father taught me everything before that. I finished middle school, so I can read the fertilizer bags and talk to the input dealer, but I trust what I see with my own eyes more than what strangers tell me. Last year urea got expensive, but I still used my usual amounts because cutting back is too risky — a bad harvest means I lose real money, while extra fertilizer is just a cost I can handle since my son sends some wages back from his factory job in Shijiazhuang.

I have 6 mu total. Three mu I put to wheat in winter and then maize in summer — that is the standard double crop around here, and you cannot miss the planting window after wheat harvest. The other three mu I plant cotton, that is my cash crop, where I make my real money. My wife helps, and my grandson does the spraying now since my back is not what it used to be. We hire pickers for the cotton in autumn, 80 yuan per day plus meals.

For the wheat: I use an improved variety, about 12 kg of seed per mu. I hire the rotary tiller from the village machine guy for 35 yuan per mu before planting. I put down one 50 kg bag of compound fertilizer per mu — the 15-15-15 kind from the dealer — and then at jointing I top-dress with half a 50 kg bag of urea per mu, so that is 25 kg. The dealer calculates it is about 17 kg nitrogen per mu total, 8 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium. I irrigate three times from my well: after planting if the soil is dry, at jointing, and at grain filling. The electricity for pumping costs me about 18 yuan each time per mu. I spray pesticide twice, once for aphids and once for powdery mildew if it shows up. I got 450 kg per mu last year, and I expect the same this year if the spring rain comes.

For the maize: I plant hybrid seed, about 2.5 kg per mu, right after the wheat comes out in early June, no time to waste. I use the rotary tiller again quick between crops, another 35 yuan per mu. I put one 40 kg bag of compound per mu at planting, and then at the big trumpet leaf stage I put another 15 kg of urea. That is about 16 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu. Maize needs less fuss than wheat. I irrigate twice: once after planting and once when the grain is filling. Two pesticide sprays. Last year I got 550 kg per mu, and I am hoping for that again.

For the cotton: This is where I spend the most because it pays the best. I use hybrid seeds, about 1.5 kg per mu. Cotton needs deep tillage, so I plough it in autumn and again in spring — I pay the tractor 50 yuan per mu for ploughing. I put more fertilizer: one 50 kg bag of compound per mu at planting, then I top-dress twice with urea, about 15 kg each time. The dealer told me cotton needs extra potassium, so I also buy potassium fertilizer and put 10 kg per mu. Total nitrogen is about 22 kg per mu, 9 kg phosphorus, 10 kg potassium. I irrigate four times: at planting, at flowering, at boll setting, and once more in August if it is dry. Cotton bollworm is my enemy, so I spray five times — I do not skip sprays on cotton, losing bolls is worse than wasting spray. Last year I got 300 kg per mu of seed cotton, and that is what I am aiming for.

I watch what Old Wang and Old Zhang do on both sides of my land. Wang uses a bit more fertilizer, Zhang uses less. I split the difference. I spent about 850 yuan per mu on cotton inputs last year and about 520 on the grain crops. With my grandson helping spray and hired hands picking, I can manage the 3 mu of cotton. I will not change much from last year — change is risky at my age, and I would rather spend a little too much on fertilizer than wake up to a bad harvest.
